title: Penn State CB pledge Deonte Flemings Jr.’s commitment is ‘strong’ after wrapping up junior season
author: Andrew Deal | Wrestling Editor
description:
4-star cornerback Deonte Flemings Jr. was the first player to make a pledge to the Nittany Lions under Matt Campbell, committing to Penn State on Jan. 31.

While he’s taken other visits during the 2026 season, Flemings still remains committed to Penn State, proving how strong the relationships he’s built with the coaching staff.

“My commitment is, I'm strong,” Flemings told The Daily Collegian. “I wouldn't have committed there if I didn't see myself going there. I built relationships over the years, and I feel great.”

Some of those relationships come from ones he’s had for multiple years, including Terry Smith, while others he’s built quicker, like with Campbell, who got him to commit to the Nittany Lions within two months of being the head coach.

Flemings said he’s “got great relationships” with the staff, and the coaches call him when they can to check in on the in-state product.

“Terry Smith, he built a relationship over the years with me,” Flemings said. “Right out of middle school, he started recruiting me my ninth grade year. Coach Campbell, he's a new guy from Iowa State, but great guy, really down to earth guy. I can't wait to be on campus and get to know those guys personally.”

The No. 5 player in Pennsylvania in the 2028 class understands the rich history the Penn State program has, something that Campbell has often mentioned since being with the Nittany Lions.

“Happy Valley is a place you want to be, definitely for school, development and also just you know building relationships,” Flemings said. “So it's a great school, a traditional school. It's a school you would want to be at.”

The McDowell product finished up his junior campaign with the Trojans after they fell to State College, 46-14, at Memorial Field, just two miles down the road from Beaver Stadium, his future home field.

“I wish we could have come out with the dub, but somebody gotta win, and the guys stay positive, and it felt great,” Flemings said. “(State College is) a great city, man. It's not that big, but it's just like where I'm from.”

Flemings saw himself grow the most through his leadership and “showing up for my team when they need me.”

On the field, he’s recognized key details as a cornerback that he’s developed as the season’s gone along, proving to be one of the top defensive backs in the nation.

“Being more patient at the line, and more patient in my backpedal, and actually reading the receivers movements,” Flemings said on details he’s improved on this season.

The Nittany Lion commit still has a little over 13 months until he’ll officially be enrolled at Penn State, where he’ll take that time to “get college ready.”

title: Penn State men's hockey drops series opener to No. 2 Michigan, remains winless in conference play
author: Sawyer Klasnick | For the Collegian
description:
Penn State, coming off being swept at home by Notre Dame last weekend, faced its toughest test of the season Friday night at Yost Ice Arena against No. 2 Michigan. Despite a late push, an early 3-0 deficit was too much to overcome as the Nittany Lions lost 6-3, dropping to 2-8-1 this season and 0-4-1 in Big Ten play.

This was the first meeting between these two teams since the semifinals of the Big Ten tournament last spring, in which the Wolverines won 5-2 on their way to a fourth Big Ten tournament championship, the most in the conference's history.

Friday also featured a rematch between goaltenders Josh Fleming and Jack Ivankovic, who were both freshmen when they squared off in last year’s postseason.

This year’s Michigan team is arguably even better than its conference championship squad. The Wolverines boast the nation’s two leading scorers in Michael Hage and Jayden Perron, not to mention freshman defenseman Landon DuPont, the projected No. 1 pick in the 2027 NHL Draft. They improved to 9-1-0 following their win Friday night.

Michigan scored just 1:42 into the game when Jack Nesbitt tipped a point shot from Ben Robertson past Fleming. Nesbitt, a 6-foot-5 first-round pick of the Flyers in the 2025 NHL Draft, was centering the third line for the Wolverines, showcasing the depth that Michigan has in addition to its star power.

Less than two minutes later, the Wolverines made it 2-0 on another deflection. This time, defenseman Drew Schock jumped in the play and positioned himself on the back door as DuPont flashed his pedigree, threading a perfect shot-pass onto Schock’s tape for an easy finish.

The early onslaught continued when Rangers draft pick Malcolm Spence scored on the power play to make it 3-0, with Michigan’s dynamic duo, Hage and Perron, picking up assists. Just seven minutes into the first period, the country’s highest-scoring offense had scored three goals, while Penn State had managed just one shot.

Despite the disastrous start, Penn State didn’t back down. The Nittany Lions got an opportunity to respond when Nesbitt was called for head contact after delivering a hit on Andrew Kuzma, sending the blue and white to the power play.

Penn State had struggled on the power play early in the season but went 3-for-6 on the man advantage last weekend against Notre Dame. The Nittany Lions carried that momentum into Ann Arbor, as Justin Poirier sniped a wrist shot past Ivankovic to cut the deficit to two.

The goal extended Poirier’s point streak to a career-long eight games and marked his team-leading sixth goal of the season. The Maine transfer was fourth in the country last season in points among freshmen and has taken another step forward in his sophomore campaign.

Following Poirier's goal, Michigan regained control of the game for the remainder of the period. However, Penn State tightened up defensively, surviving lengthy shifts in its own zone and getting several crucial saves from Fleming to keep the score at 3-1.

Penn State officially made it a contest on the second shift of the second period when Kale Dach found an open Shea Busch in transition. The freshman forward then beat Ivankovic over his glove.

Josh Fleming made consecutive ridiculous saves on two separate Michigan odd-man rushes early in the second period, taking goals away from Hage and Perron, respectively.

Just as it looked like Penn State had turned the tide, Aidan Park scored Michigan’s fourth goal of the night, redirecting a shot from Schock. The goal was Park’s first of the season.

Penn State forward Lev Katzin was called for a slash while backchecking a 3-on-2 with 2:30 to play in the second period, but Penn State’s conference-best penalty kill stood tall. Then, Wolverine forward Cole McKinney took an offensive zone penalty in the period’s final minute, opening the door for a Nittany Lion comeback.

Michigan killed off the McKinney penalty, but the Penn State push continued.

Captain Reese Laubach has owned Michigan in his career at Penn State, scoring 11 goals in 14 games entering Friday. He added number 12 on a 2-on-1 just under four minutes into the third period, making it a 4-3 game.

With 12:54 to play, it looked as if Justin Larose had tied the game when he ripped a one-timer into the back of the net. However, after review, the goal was called back for being offside.

The Nittany Lion momentum was halted following the disallowed goal, and the Michigan defense clamped down. Ivankovic was rarely tested in the game’s final ten minutes, despite being busy most of the night.

With 1:59 remaining, Nick Moldenhauer restored the Wolverines’ two-goal lead when a shot from the point changed direction and bounced right onto his stick. He buried it behind a helpless Fleming to seal the Michigan victory.

Ben Robertson finished the scoring with an empty-netter, sealing the Wolverines’ 6-3 win.

Up Next

Penn State will play the second game of the series against Michigan on Saturday at 7 p.m. at Yost Ice Arena.

title: Four-goal second period propels No. 7 Penn State women’s hockey to 7-2 win over AHA rival Mercyhurst
author: Brady Welsh | For the Collegian
description:
No. 7 Penn State women’s hockey defeated the Mercyhurst Lakers by a final score of 7-2 in game one of a two-game AHA series at Mercyhurst Ice Center this weekend. It was the first time the two teams met since the Nittany Lions’ 3-2 AHA Championship victory at Pegula Ice Arena last season.

Penn State began the game with a huge chance in front on the backhand by Kylie Amelkovich, but it was met by the pad of Mercyhurst goalie Grace Kipfer.

The save seemed to spring the Lakers, who started putting pressure on and capitalized. Under four minutes into the game, Mariia Polozkova, looking through a sea of bodies in the slot, found Maja Alenius across the crease for a tap-in goal to give Mercyhurst an early 1-0 lead. It was the first of Alenius’ sophomore campaign.

Penn State kept pressure after the goal, but were denied by Kipfer every time. With under eight minutes to go, the Nittany Lions were called for icing twice in a row on missed passes. The second cost them big. The Lakers won the faceoff and Polozkova took a shot. Alenius crashed the net and buried the rebound for her second of the period, and Mercyhurst’s second of the game.

Megan Hosman took a holding penalty with six minutes left to play in the first, giving the Lakers their first power play.

The power play was cut short after Berlin Lolacher went to the box for cross-checking and Penn State got a minute power play of its own, and didn’t waste it. The Nittany Lions got the puck to the crease and Amelkovich was there to shovel it in for her fifth goal of the season to cut the deficit in half, 2-1.

With a little over a minute left in the period, Outwater got another breakaway chance, but wasn’t able to put it home again, as Kipfer made a spread-eagled save along the left post. Mercyhurst got one more chance before the end of the period, but Maddy Campbell made the save. The Lakers kept a 2-1 lead going into the second.

Both teams had opportunities to cash in an early goal in the first five minutes of the second period, and were held scoreless until Amelkovich and Outwater went on a two-on-one. Amelkovich took the shot off the pad of Kipfer, but Outwater was there to put home the rebound, tying the game at two with her team-leading ninth goal of the season.

The Nittany Lions had all of the momentum in the first half of the second period as four minutes later, Mikah Keller led another Penn State odd-man rush, opted to keep it, and found the top left corner to beat Kipfer for the Nittany Lions’ third unanswered goal to take a 3-2 lead.

Penn State got yet another two-on-one opportunity and Lolacher brought down McKenna Walsh along the boards as she was attempting to receive a cross-ice pass from outwater, being sent to the sin bin for the second time.

Unlike in the first, the Lakers were able to kill this one off, thanks to Kipfer, who made two great saves halfway through the power play to take away a prime scoring chance as Keller found Danica Maynard all alone across the ice, who got padded away, then Alanna Devlin tried shoveling the rebound in the crease that was quickly covered up and out of harm’s way to keep it a one-goal game.

With 2:48 left in the period, Maynard took a penalty to put the Lakers on another power play, but this one was short-lived as well. Julia Perjus went to the box 38 seconds into the man advantage for unsportsmanlike conduct, taking the game to its second four-on-four.

Outwater took the puck off Abby Poitras and got a tipped pass back to the point for Ashley Kokavec, who sent it across to Hosman, who blasted it past Kipfer with one second remaining before a Nittany Lions power play. The Nittany Lions scored their fourth of the period 40 seconds later on that power play, as Maynard took a shot from the left circle that deflected off the stick of Devlin and in for the Boston College transfer’s first goal in the blue and white, while allowing Penn State to come out of the second period with a 5-2 lead.

It was the first time Penn State had scored four in a period on the road since Feb. 1, 2025, at Robert Morris.

Mercyhurst came out on fire in the third, with a two-on-one chance denied by Campbell. Perjus took another penalty, this time for tripping and the Nittany Lions went on their fourth power play looking to stay perfect, and they did. Sophie Morrow got it to Sofia Ismael in the right circle. The freshman who leads Penn State in points sniped it past Kipfer for her seventh goal and 17th point of the year, and sixth unanswered goal of the night for the Nittany Lions.

However, they still weren’t satisfied. With 4:27 left in the game, Ismael, Abby Stonehouse and Keller went on a three-on-one, with Stonehouse getting it to Keller, who quickly got the puck back to her for a tap-in goal courtesy of some gorgeous passing, making it a 7-2 game. The Nittany Lions earned their 10th win of the season, and it was the first time they had seven different goal scorers in a game since Nov. 14, 2025, almost a year to the day.

Up Next

Penn State will play Mercyhurst for game two of this series at 1 p.m. Saturday.

title: Minnesota team stuck in state due to nationwide ground stop ahead of Saturday game against Penn State
author: Lexie Linderman | Football Editor
description:
Minnesota is currently stuck in Minneapolis ahead of its Saturday matchup against Penn State after a nationwide groundstop was instituted by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

The Nittany Lions are not expecting the game, which is set to kickoff at 7 p.m. Saturday, to be cancelled or postponed, according to reporting by the Centre Daily Times.

“The University of Minnesota football was on its charter flight about to depart for Penn State when the FAA nationwide ground stoppage went into effect. As a result, the Gophers were unable to travel to Penn State on Friday for Saturday’s game. Minnesota has been in communication with the Big Ten and Penn State and will provide relevant updates as necessary,” a Minnesota spokesperson said.

Penn State issued a statement that read it “is in communication with the Big Ten Conference and the University of Minnesota. We will continue to closely monitor the situation and will share updates when available.”

It’s a 14-hour drive from Minnesota to State College. With kickoff under 24 hours away, it’s unclear whether the Golden Gophers would go that route if no updates regarding the groundstop are provided. Purdue is driving to its matchup at Iowa, which is about a five-hour trip.

The Big Ten handles any postponements or cancellations on a case-by-case rule, working with affected athletics departments and networks to determine the best course of action.

Other schools affected include Washington, Texas, Tennessee, Ole Miss and Tulane.

title: Nationwide ground stop lifted, FAA says, 5 hours after it was initiated
author: Neel Ved | The Daily Collegian
description:
Editor's Note: This story was updated Friday evening when the ground stop was lifted.

The nationwide ground stop issued by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has been lifted, according to Markwayne Mullin, the secretary of homeland security, and Sean Duffy, the transportation secretary, who spoke to the media at the White House Friday evening.

Mullin reiterated an FAA's spokesperson's earlier statement that it was a communications problem impacting Air Route Traffic Control Centers, which are responsible for overseeing flights across the country.

The ground stop was initiated at 3:36 p.m., according to the FAA, which cited “extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety." Inbound international flights were being determined on a case-by-case basis.

This is the third time there has ever been a nationwide ground stop. The most recent stop was in January 2023, when a pilot notification system had gone down. The other ground stop followed the Sept. 11, 2001 attacks.

title: Penn State Board of Trustees vote to sell York campus
author: Curtis Johnson | For the Collegian
description:
The Penn State Board of Trustees (BoT) voted to sell the Penn State York campus following the campus’s spring 2027 closure on Friday. York College of Pennsylvania will purchase the campus for $7.4 million.

The vote followed approval from the Finance and Investment Committee on Thursday. All trustees voted in favor, except for Cynthia Dunn, Russell Redding and Carrie Rowe who abstained.

In the sale, the York campus will be developed to support health sciences opportunities at York College, with collaboration from WellSpan health and the York County Economic Alliance.

Penn State is set to close the York campus alongside other Commonwealth Campuses for the 2027-2028 academic year, including DuBois, Fayette, Mont Alto, New Kensington, Shenango Wilkes-Barre.

The York campus sale follows the Penn State Shenango and Wilkes-Barre in September.

title: LionPATH to be offline this weekend for scheduled maintenance
author: Kevin Harris | For the Collegian
description:
LionPATH, Penn State’s official student information system, will be down this weekend due to scheduled maintenance, according to an email sent to users at Penn State.

From Nov. 14, 12:01 a.m. to Nov. 15, 11:59 a.m, the system will be unavailable to all users. The LionPATH Development and Maintenance Organization will use this time to complete a necessary system upgrade from the software vendor, Oracle.

During this time, all users including students, faculty and staff will be unable to send or receive data from the LionPATH system.

LionPATH, which replaced ISIS (Integrated Student Information System) and its front end web portal eLion in 2016 is the main way students use to enroll in classes, manage academic records, and view financial aid awards.

Once LionPATH is back online, users may notice minor changes to the interface, however, most of the changes will be internal to ensure continued support from Oracle and user transparency.

This downtime window will begin just two minutes after the late drop deadline on Nov. 13, 11:59 p.m.

title: Penn State women’s basketball prepares for toughest test yet against Arizona State
author: Noah Radio | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State is looking to flip the script against Arizona State on Sunday. The 0-3 Lady Lions travel to Tempe to battle the 3-0 Sun Devils.

The Lady Lions haven’t found much success on either end of the court early in the season. They kicked off the road trip with a 23-point drubbing by Cincinnati.

On Monday, Penn State jumped out to a hot start against Dayton, but ultimately lost, 77-71. The Lady Lions were able to pull more positives out of the battle with the Flyers than in either of the previous two losses.

The Big Ten Media Day duo of Petra Božan and Devyn Quigley each posted career highs on the scoreboard. Božan led all scorers with 27 points on 10-for-11 shooting. The Split, Croatia native also knocked down a career-best five of her six three-point attempts.

Quigley, an NC State transfer, scored 23 points and was also hot from beyond the arc. The junior put up 18 of her points on three-pointers, and she added five rebounds, three assists and three steals.

One additional storyline to watch this weekend is the Penn State starting lineup. Against Cleveland State and Cincinnati, Tanisha Wright rolled out Quigley, Božan, Enjulina Gonzalez, Savannah White and Ava Black. In the Monday matchup, Wright replaced White and Black with Skylar Durley and Cristen Carter.

Durley, the 2025-26 Mountain West Freshman of the Year, trailed only Quigley in minutes and scored 10 points on 12 shots.

Carter has led the Lady Lions in two of the first three contests. Her defense was on full display against Dayton as she locked up the Flyers’ star center, Fatima Ibrahim. Wright will need to concoct the right combination, with her squad’s toughest test to date coming on Sunday.

Arizona State has not lost a regular-season nonconference game since Molly Miller took over before the 2025 season. The Sun Devils went 15-0 in nonconference play last season, including a 74-60 victory over the Lady Lions in Happy Valley.

This year, the maroon and gold are 3-0 and coming off a 65-58 road win over UNLV. The Rebels were overwhelmingly picked first in the Mountain West in the league’s preseason poll. In the first two games of the campaign, the Aztecs blew out Jackson State and Northern Arizona.

Ruby Whitehorn leads Arizona State in nearly every category. The senior leads the team in points per game and blocks with 14.7 and five, respectively. Whitehorn, a Tennessee transfer, is tied for the team lead in rebounds with 23 and sits at second in assists.

The former five-star recruit spent her first two years at Clemson before starting 28 of 34 games for the Volunteers last season.

The Aztecs are also strong in the frontcourt. Forwards Heloisa Carrera and McKinna Brackens each average over 10 points and five rebounds per game.

When Penn State touches down in Tempe, it'll be the final flight of its road trip. The Lady Lions return home to face Bowling Green and Saint Joseph’s next week. But first, they tipoff their upset bid against Arizona State at 4 p.m. on Sunday.

title: Penn State vs. Minnesota preview | Forecast, betting odds ahead of battle for bowl eligibility
author: Andrew Mercer | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State returns home to Beaver Stadium at 7 p.m. Saturday to host Minnesota in Week 11. Both teams are 5-4 overall, but the Nittany Lions are game behind the Golden Gophers in Big Ten play, coming in at 2-4 in the conference compared to their opponent’s 3-3.

With a pair of teams duking it out for bowl eligibility, here’s everything you need to know heading into the game.

Forecast

Make sure to dress for the cold — and potentially the season’s first snowfall — as Saturday’s forecast includes a high of 42 and a low of 31 degrees, according to AccuWeather.

At kickoff, the temperature will be 36 degrees with a real feel of 23 accompanied by 15 mph winds trending north or northwest, threatening to blow rain and snow around.

The precipitation should stop after about an hour, and the temperature will only drop to 35 degrees by 11 p.m.

Betting, how to watch

The Nittany Lions enter Week 11 as 9.5-point favorites in Happy Valley, according to FanDuel.

With an over/under set at 41.5, the sportsbooks expect a 25-16 Penn State victory, qualifying the team for a bowl.

The game will be broadcast on Fox Sports 1, and tickets can be found as low as $11 on Ticketmaster.

About Minnesota

The Golden Gophers have had a tough two-game stretch since their victory over then-No. 15 Iowa, playing Indiana and UCLA back-to-back. While they kept the games relatively close, taking the Hoosiers to overtime, the team is on a two-game losing streak heading into Week 11.

However, coach PJ Fleck’s squad suffered a 41-13 blowout upset to Purdue, making the Golden Gophers one of the Big Ten’s biggest wild cards.

Minnesota has the worst rushing offense in the Big Ten, averaging just 98.6 yards per game, and has the No. 14-ranked pass game, with an average of 209 yards per game.

The team is led by quarterback Drake Lindsey, who has 1,797 passing yards, 11 touchdowns and seven interceptions on the season. His main target is wide receiver Javon Tracy, who has 485 receiving yards and one touchdown.

However, wide receivers Noah Jennings and Jalen Smith aren’t too far behind with 421 and 348 receiving yards, respectively. Smith’s three touchdowns are the team’s most through the air.

Running backs TJ Thomas and Darius Taylor have distinct roles in the run game. Thomas is the leading rusher with an even 400 rushing yards and a touchdown, while Taylor is primarily an end zone threat with a team-high six touchdowns on just 263 rushing yards.

Minnesota’s pass defense ranks No. 8, and its run defense ranks No. 10 in the conference.

Linebacker Maverick Baranowski is the Golden Gophers’ top defender with a team-high 69 tackles and two interceptions. Defensive lineman TJ Bush Jr. is the biggest threat in the pass rush with six sacks.

About Penn State

After starting conference play 0-3, Penn State has gotten back on track with consecutive victories over Purdue and Washington.

This resurgence has sparked from an increased emphasis on the run game, with the success of running backs Carson Hansen and Cam Wallace leading the way. Both have logged an 100-yard performance in the past two weeks, as the Nittany Lions now have the No. 7 rushing offense in the Big Ten.

Hansen leads Penn State in the run game with 493 rushing yards and six touchdowns, finding the end zone in five straight games. He’s followed by Wallace’s 316 rushing yards and four touchdowns, currently on a two-game scoring streak.

Meanwhile, the Nittany Lions’ passing offense ranks No. 6 in the Big Ten, with Rocco Becht finding more consistency through the air since his two interceptions at Michigan. Becht has 2,079 passing yards, 15 touchdowns and five interceptions on the season, averaging 231 yards per game.

Wide receiver Chase Sowell is Becht’s primary target in the passing game with 635 receiving yards and four touchdowns. With Koby Howard once again out for Saturday, Sowell’s the likely catalyst for the Nittany Lions’ passing offense.

Penn State has the No. 1 pass defense in the conference, led by cornerbacks Audavion Collins and Daryus Dixson. The Nittany Lions only allow an average of 144.3 yards per game through the air.

However, Penn State has struggled in the run defense all season long, ranking 16th in the Big Ten. While the Nittany Lions have bounced back from Northwestern, which ran for over 400 yards, missed tackles continue to be an area of concern.

title: Dominic Fike releases new album 'HOW TO QUIT SMOKING'
author: Brennan Kramp I The Daily Collegian
description:
Dominic Fike recently released his third studio album, “HOW TO QUIT SMOKING,” on Oct. 30. The album is a quintessential Fike sound: lo-fi beats, sunny guitar riffs and a nonchalant rap style that drips through each track like gentle rain — or tears.

On “HOW TO QUIT SMOKING,” we see Fike spill his heart out even more than we have on his previous hit albums like 2023’s “Sunburn” and 2020’s “What Could Possibly Go Wrong.” After turning 30, Fike seems to be trying to leave behind his angsty 20s and take advantage of some of what life has to offer by being a pop superstar but is still held down by the trials of his come up.

Fike has not had a traditional musician's career. He’s had quite the inverse: In 2016, Fike was arrested after an altercation with a Florida police officer and was sentenced to house arrest where he began working on his demo EP “Don’t Forget About Me, Demos.”

In 2018, while being incarcerated for violating his house arrest and failing a drug test at the age of 22, Fike’s demo was released on SoundCloud by his friend. This sparked a major label bidding war which inevitably landed him a $4 million deal with Columbia Records after he was released.

His introduction into the mainstream came swift and was a startling adjustment for someone fresh out of jail. The pressure he felt to produce as a bold, new, pop artist must have been immense and was heard deeply on his initial projects.

We hear Fike trying to come to grips with his adulthood, fatherhood and the new trials he faces in a world that he has earned all by himself. The album's title alone is a perfect introduction to what Fike really wants to say. He’s trying to get better — one habit at a time, one day at a time, one thought at a time.

Trying to control his addictive personality is a common and relatable theme in his discography that has been one of the many aspects that draw fans to his music. Tracks like “CABBY” and “PANGEA,” delve into this desire to right past wrongs with these addictions and the people he’s hurt from them.

Fike has a distinct longing in his voice with every track on this album. There's a sense that he is trying to be as strong as possible while still hinting that he needs all the help he can get.

On “WHITE KEYS” and “WAR MACHINE,” Fike takes aim at what life is like trying to be both an international music star while still feeling like a broken watch stuck on the same time a few years back.

Sure, he has his money, his fame and his dreams, that were probably shaped more while in the cold confines of a Florida jail, coming true. Nonetheless, the criticisms don’t stop no matter how much of his heart he puts on his sleeve. Yet he persists through the pain: “I hate to let everyone here down / But that’s life / Some people get their kicks by stomping on my dreams / But they’re just mean,” Fike raps on "WAR MACHINE."

“CASTING CALL” is Fike’s attempt at reaching out for something, or someone, that will take the pain away without dealing double afterwards. Sobriety is not something people can do alone. Fike knows this. He’s no stranger to that struggle, and this track, along with the album in its entirety, is him trying to make that clear.

What’s grimly comforting about an album like this is that it's both reflective and supportive. His songs are both confessions and lessons. Fike is pleading with his listeners to take his anxiety and his struggle for all their worth and learn from them rather than pity him.

To go along with a powerful message, Fike collaborates with eight other artists on the album to give his sound a brighter feeling that adds a refreshing sparkle to the rest of the album.

His Jack Johnson-esque guitar work blends perfectly with his traditionally passive and almost ambient beats in some tracks while still kicking up the tempo on the intro song “WALLFLOWER” as well as “DOOMSDAY.”

The closing track, “SPOTLIGHT / INNER CHILD,” sees Fike collaborating with tapes sent by rapper Tay-K, who is currently serving an 80-year prison sentence for robbery and murder. A controversial choice some might say, but the bold juxtaposition in their lyrics is worth the creative risk.

While Fike wraps up the album with a simplistic summary of everything that’s been played in the 38 minutes prior, Tay-K talks about his brief life before prison and the days ahead: nostalgia, childhood trauma and his mother.

This closing track allows both Fike and the listener to take a closer examination at their own lives. It's a tough world, and there’s a laundry list of things that everyone wants to better themselves on.

However, what Fike does here with his concluding message is show that while you may hope to achieve everything you want all at once, all you need is the perspective to see that you don’t need to. You have the time, so take it and just keep doing your best.

title: Players to watch | QB Drake Lindsey, trio of receivers lead Minnesota’s pass-reliant offense
author: Noah Aberegg | The Daily Collegian
description:
For the second straight week, Penn State will face a pass-first offense when Minnesota comes to town for a 7 p.m. matchup in Beaver Stadium.

The Golden Gophers are led by quarterback Drake Lindsey, who’s found success targeting a series of wide receivers. Defensively, they’re a middle-of-the-pack team in the Big Ten, giving up the eighth-most passing yards per game and 10th-most yards on the ground.

Here’s some players to watch for Minnesota.

Drake Lindsey, quarterback

Lindsey has put the Golden Gophers’ offense on his back, accounting for 64.9% of their total yards this season.

However, he’s been far from perfect, with only 11 touchdowns through nine games. Lindsey has thrown for multiple scores just twice this year and has seven interceptions, the second-most in the conference.

While he accounts for a majority of Minnesota’s offense, his total passing yardage sits 10th in the Big Ten. Against then-No. 4 Indiana, he threw for just 120 yards.

Lindsey’s inability to run has resulted in him being sacked 10 times. He was brought down four times against the Hoosiers and three times against Iowa the week before.

Aydan West, defensive back

Despite only being a sophomore, Aydan West has taken the Big Ten by storm as one of the best defensive backs this season.

West has the second-most passes deflected in the conference with nine. He also had an interception against Michigan, leaping along the sideline to pick off quarterback Bryce Underwood.

The star defensive back also has 20 solo tackles and 13 assisted tackles.

Against Mississippi State in Week 2, West recorded a fumble recovery and touchdown after quarterback Kamario Taylor was hit and coughed up the ball.

West will have a big role on Saturday, as he’ll likely be paired against Penn State wide receiver Chase Sowell throughout the game. Sowell has 15 receptions for 276 yards and two touchdowns over his last two games.

TJ Bush Jr., defensive lineman

TJ Bush Jr. has been a menace through Big Ten play, recording five sacks in six conference games played so far.

While he’ll be looking to take down Rocco Becht on Saturday, he’s found success against much more active quarterbacks this year. Bush had two sacks against Underwood when the Golden Gophers took on Michigan and one on Washington gunslinger Demond Williams Jr.

But Bush has done more than just terrorize opposing quarterbacks, forcing a fumble, recovering one and tallying an interception this year.

Javon Tracy, wide receiver

While Minnesota has two wide receivers with over 400 yards and another that leads the team in touchdowns, Javon Tracy has emerged as the biggest threat.

Tracy leads the team with 485 yards on 49 receptions this year. He has four games with seven receptions each, one of which came against Indiana.

However, he’s only found the end zone once this season, scoring against Washington in Week 4.

D’Anton Lynn was asked about Tracy on Tuesday, in which he responded, “He's an outstanding threat. We have to know where he's at at all times.”

Maverick Baranowski, linebacker

In his fifth year at Minnesota, Maverick Baranowski has made plays all over the field, leading the team with 37 solo tackles and 32 assisted tackles. He also recorded an interception against Williams.

Baranowski has made some of his biggest plays against the top teams in the conference, forcing and recovering a fumble against Iowa on Oct. 24 and forcing another fumble against Indiana a week later.

title: Budget-friendly meals college students can make at home
author: Talia Rittenhouse | The Daily Collegian
description:
College students are always looking for quick, easy, cheap meals they can make at home.

Funds can become tight for students who try to budget their summer income across eight months of school. And when they turn 21, this budget will seem even smaller every day.

It’s difficult for some students to get a job to help off-set these costs because of their busy schedules. Students balance 15-credit semesters, club meetings, extracurriculars and more.

If you’re looking for cheaper meals to eat during the year, and are over the “no-grocery-store challenge,” you might want to keep reading so you stay full on a college budget.

Sheet-pan meals

These are some of the simplest dishes you can make! You start by picking out your favorite protein, vegetables and a starch, like fan-favorite, sweet potatoes. Then, you cut them all up and toss in olive oil and as many seasonings as your heart desires.

All of these ingredients go into the oven on one cooking sheet for about 30 minutes or until they're cooked through, depending on the protein being used.

Not only is this meal quick and easy to make, but by purchasing whole foods, and utilizing spices and oil you most likely have in your kitchen, your bank account won’t be crying like when you order takeout. This meal is also great for meal-prepping, which is a great time-saver when it comes to busy college life.

Chicken caesar wrap

Who doesn’t like a chicken Caesar wrap? This meal seems to be everyone’s go-to for a lunch out with friends. (With fries and a crisp Diet Coke, of course.)

Well, college students no longer have to wait to go to an expensive restaurant or Cafe 210 West to have their favorite dish. With $2 Caesar dressing and tortillas, $3 lettuce and an $8 large pack of chicken breasts from Aldi, students can make this meal for days on end before running out of ingredients, saving money and trips to the grocery store

Taco bowls

We’re bringing Chipotle home. Now, before you say “it just isn’t the same,” I sadly already know that, as a frequent Chipotle connoisseur myself. But my bank account doesn’t allow me to go there as often as I’d like, unless it’s on someone else’s dime.

These taco bowls can be made easily with ground chicken, which at Giant, students can purchase right now on sale for $3.19, or splurge a little more for ground beef.

And the fun doesn’t end there. Students can fully customize these bowls with toppings of their choosing. Personally, I’d recommend cheese, sour cream, lettuce, tomatoes and a container of rice to complete the bowl. For seasonings, students can grab Old El Paso original taco seasoning mix for $1 packet or a container of it for $3.99 for 35 servings worth of taco bowl meals.

Garlic butter shrimp pasta

After a quick scroll on Pinterest, I came across a recipe for garlic butter shrimp pasta that only takes 15 minutes. This reminded me of the shrimp scampi or lemon shrimp pasta I would have at home, and I realized that I could even make a dish that feels so fancy and complicated here while at school.

Many students don’t think of having shrimp for dinner, but it’s another great protein source for when you're sick of having chicken with every meal.

Buying frozen shrimp also saves you money in the long run, as this one-time $11 purchase at Giant can lead you to many dinners in the future. While at the store, don’t forget to buy some pasta, butter, garlic cloves (or preminced “jarlic”), lemon, parsley and any other seasonings you might want if you don’t have an assortment at home.

Yogurt bowls

Yogurt bowls can be as simple or as extravagant as you desire. At most of State College’s local grocery stores, students can purchase individual containers of yogurt or a large container to have over the course of a few days.

This meal allows students to adjust ingredients to fit their budget by deciding what fruits, granola or additional toppings to add to accommodate their needs.

Some of my favorites are chopped strawberries, blueberries and honey paired with the variety of granolas carried at Trader Joe’s. Being able to customize this breakfast, lunch or snack, allows you to mix up your meals over the week, all while following a college-friendly budget.

title: Books that deserve a film adaptation
author: Rebecca Fein | The Daily Collegian
description:
As Penn State’s fall foliage finally turns brown and the sun sets before students are done with their last lectures, it may be time to start searching for your next bingeable series.

If cozying up with a good book isn’t your “scene,” here’s a list of some reads that would become hits with a television or film adaptation.

“I Hope This Finds You Well” by Natalie Sue

“I Hope This Finds You Well,” a debut comedy novel by Natalie Sue, has won both the Stephen Leacock Memorial Medal for Humour and the Georges Bugnet Award for Fiction.

The story follows Jolene Smith, an administrative assistant at a grocery store company. Jolene, feeling isolated and lost, especially in the workplace, copes by putting snarky remarks at the bottom of her emails that she makes invisible to the recipients. After a careless slip up, Jolene is caught and forced to take sensitivity training and have her computer monitored. While her work was adding restrictions to her computer, Jolene was accidentally granted access to all employees' files and private chats.

This novel would make a great movie because of its comedic nature but also heartbreaking themes of seclusion that many college students and young adults can relate to.

There’s an ongoing romance within the story that would hook watchers immediately. Between the humor, romance and workplace drama, it gives off similar vibes as the television classic, “The Office” by Greg Daniels, a show where nine seasons was definitely not enough.

“Matched” trilogy by Allie Condie

“Matched” and its sequels “Crossed” and “Reached” by Allie Condie is a young adult novel series that follows main character, Cassia, as she embarks on the journey of a lifetime.

The dystopian series takes place years in the future, where people are living in a totalitarian society. On every person's seventeenth birthday, they attend something called “the matching banquet,” a ceremony where young adults find out who they will spend the rest of their life with.

After Ky, a boy who rebels against the system, pops up on the screen to be matched with Cassia, officials explain it as a technical error since degenerates don’t have the privilege of being matched. Chaos ensues as Cassia hunts to find Ky and discover what the system is really hiding from her.

The main character, Cassia, would be cast perfectly by Mckenna Grace, who seems unable to turn down a role lately, or even Xochitl Gomez, due to her experience with "mad" adventures through the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

The “Matched” series would make an amazing movie trilogy as it explores themes prevalent today such as individualism versus conformity and breaking social norms for the greater good of society. With the popularity of dystopian movies making a return as audiences prepare for the release of “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping,” this series could satisfy society’s need for more futuristic teen dramas.

“The Five People You Meet In Heaven” by Mitch Albom

Mitch Albom, who authored the book in which the 1999 movie, “Tuesdays with Morrie” was adapted, wrote another award-winning story that often gets overlooked.

“The Five People You Meet In Heaven” follows the story of 83-year-old Eddie, a World War II veteran, who works as an amusement park maintenance worker and feels trapped in a monotonous cycle towards the end of his life.

When he passes, Eddie goes to Heaven, and instead of the run-of-the-mill paradise people always dream about, he faces a series of different people and places that made an impact on his life. These five people help him understand his life before heading to his final destination in the afterlife.

Although this book already has a 2004 adaptation, it could use a serious modern upgrade to rework these lessons for current audiences.

This story teaches vital lessons, such as shared humanity and the idea that every action matters, no matter how unimportant it may seem.

“Pretties” by Scott Westerfeld

“Pretties” is the second novel in the “Uglies” trilogy.

The original book, “Uglies,” follows the story of Tally Youngblood, a loyal and fierce 15-year-old girl.

In Tally’s society, everybody under the age of 15 is deemed ugly, but, when people reach 16 years old, they receive a mandatory cosmetic surgery that makes them pretty.

The cosmetic surgery doesn’t just change their appearance, it puts lesions on their brain, making it hard to think critically, forcing people to become docile and easily controllable. After Tally realizes this, she fights to not get the surgery when her sixteenth birthday arrives. However, after possibly finding a cure, she voluntarily goes through with it, in hopes that the cure will work. “Pretties” follows the aftermath of Tally’s decision.

“Uglies” was released on Netflix in 2024, starring Joey King and Chase Stokes. The movie was received with mixed reviews online, but Netflix has still not confirmed a sequel. Fans of the trilogy and first movie are dying to see how “Pretties” will play out on the big screen.

Although these books may never get the movie adaptation they deserve, we can read them over and over again to the point where, when we close our eyes, our own version of the movie plays.

title: Column | Penn State men’s soccer official report card in coach Rob Dow’s first year
author: Ava Aguilar | The Daily Collegian
description:
The first season of the Dow era is officially over after the Nittany Lions dropped their final match against Maryland last week, 2-0.

While it had a bumpy start, Penn State was able to see some success towards the end, despite its season being marked with more losses than victories.

Here’s how I’d grade Dow’s first rebuilding year.

Overall season: C+

Performance/Wins: D

Perhaps the most difficult thing about Penn State’s season this year was watching its matches play out the same way every time, even though the team is stacked full of potential.

The blue and white would kick off strong, pressuring opponents and controlling the ball. All before losing steam in the second half and often missing out on wins by a last-minute goal.

They finished the season 3-9-3, starting with a win against Mercyhurst, one loss, and another win against Yale. Only to be followed by an almost month-long losing streak, until their 0-0 tie against Michigan.

The Nittany Lions were able to find their groove towards the end of the season as they racked up more ties, including their breakthrough moment with a 2-2 finish against No. 13 Wisconsin. This propelled them to their first win since September the next week against Duquesne, going 3-1 on senior day, and finally playing like the squad they had the ability to be.

Coaching: A

There is no doubt that if anybody can restore this program to its former glory, it will be Rob Dow. With his star-studded reputation, a national championship at Vermont, and an overall 149-41-21 record, Dow has the skills and experience to take the Nittany Lions all the way.

Throughout the season, players frequently remarked on Dow’s motivational coaching abilities and genuine care for the team. All of which played a role in the team’s drive and determination on the field.

In an interview on Oct. 1, midfielder Grant McIntosh told The Daily Collegian that “It’s rare to have a coach that really cares about you as a person, " he said, “(He) demands the best of you day in and day out.”

Offense: B

The team is stacked on offense, with players like Etienne Reck dominating in shots and goals and often being the one to put points on the board.

Along with Reck came players like Joe Sheridan and Amadou Kone, who also played a large role on offense, with the three totaling nine goals in the season.

However, foul play and yellow cards were one downside of the Nittany Lion offense, with 33 total yellows issued throughout the season. All of which would typically end in the team giving up points off of avoidable corners and free kicks.

Defense: C

Although Penn State had a stacked defensive roster, their inability to play hard for the full 90 minutes left keeper Daniel Peluffo-Wiese working overtime and needing to step up to avoid getting demolished.

This was most evident in their game against Wisconsin, where Peluffo-Wiese tallied a career-high nine saves and allowed only two goals.

However, Joe Sheridan and Noah Förster were two starters and forces to be reckoned with on the field, both playing important roles in keeping their box free from any opposing offenders.

Recruiting: A

Dow built his team from the ground up, coming in with only three returning players from the original roster.

He was able to recruit major names like Reck and earn the trust of former players at Vermont to follow him to Happy Valley, bringing along Toby Grant and former Catamount recruit Dylan Mirakian.

Dow also brought over his two former assistant coaches, Brad Cole and Owen Jack, who have been part of Dow’s award-winning staff since 2023 and 2025, respectively.

It will be interesting to see what names he is able to bring in for the next season, but he has already secured the No. 1 recruit in Pennsylvania with defender Mateo Gallegos.

title: ‘I enjoyed the moment’ | Penn State wrestling’s Luke Lilledahl starts title defense with emphatic win
author: Elliott Inscho | The Daily Collegian
description:
Nobody could beat Luke Lilledahl last season, and it took him two periods on Thursday to remind the nation why.

As a sophomore, the 125-pounder cruised to an unblemished 25-0 record en route to claiming his first NCAA title in March. In the opening bout of his title defense, Lilledahl worked efficiently to earn a tech fall over Bloomsburg’s Justin Jones to open the Nittany Lions’ first dual.

“I feel like I just went out, had fun and wrestled pretty well.” Lilledahl said.

The St. Charles, Missouri, native, scored three takedowns in the first period, cycling between shooting on the 5-foot-7 Husky’s legs and allowing him to stand back up. After three minutes, he jumped out to a 9-2 lead and started the second frame from the bottom.

He jolted to his feet in five seconds and got back to work, taking Jones down three more times to ultimately seal the 19-4 technical fall in the second period.

“(I’ve) been working on a couple different things since my last competition,” Lilledahl said. “(I have) some things to work on in certain positions. But overall, I feel like I enjoyed the moment.”

It was an interesting offseason for the reigning national champion. After winning a 2-1 decision over Princeton’s Marc-Anthony McGowan, Lilledahl went west for the U23 World Championships in Las Vegas, Nevada.

Lilledahl had claimed the tournament’s top prize in 2025, winning the gold medal in Novi Sad, Serbia. Back stateside, he entered the competition’s 2026 iteration as a favorite to defend the title with the previous win and college championship on his resume.

It wasn’t so simple. In his first match of the tournament, Lilledahl fell to Kazakhstan’s Merey Bazarbayev in a 3-1 decision. He got back on track with a 5-0 repechage defeat of France’s Rassoul Galbouraev, but finished in fifth place after Daito Katsume handed him a second 3-1 loss.

In the preseason, Lilledahl made clear that his struggles in the tournament wouldn’t affect him moving forward.

They certainly didn’t on Thursday.

“When you're at the highest level, people are gonna find things to criticize whether you win or lose, so if I would have won, I'm sure there would still be people that would be out there criticizing me,” Lilledahl said at local media day. “I don't really care what the critics have to say because I'm gonna keep getting better and I'm gonna keep enjoying the sport.”

On Sunday, Penn State will wrestle its first away dual of the year, making the trip to the McCasland Field House for a date with Oklahoma. There, Lilledahl will likely take on Sebastian Degennaro, who is 2-0 in the Sooners’ opening duals.

While it’s a long journey to Norman and a quick turnaround after Penn State’s 42-3 victory over Bloomsburg, Lilledahl doesn’t seem worried about the Nittany Lions’ ability to handle the circumstances.

“Lineup-wise, I feel like we have guys at every weight class that could compete at any given time, so an early road trip doesn't really mean as much,” Lilledahl said. “It means more for traveling, getting your weight down and wrestling in an arena that you maybe haven't wrestled in before, the atmosphere and things like that. But I don't think a lot of things change this early in the season.”

title: 'He looked pretty dang good' | Masanosuke Ono flashed in first match with scorching first period
author: Gavin Leonard | The Daily Collegian
description:
After watching the unveiling of its 2026 NCAA Championship banner, Penn State dominated in its season opener against Bloomsburg in a 42-3 win, featuring the debut of international superstar Masanosuke Ono.

Heading into Penn State’s match against Bloomsburg, the starter at 133 pounds was up in the air. Following Marcus Blaze’s move to 141, the spot was left vacant for Ono or Nate Desmond. Cael Sanderson ultimately went with Ono, who was chosen by the same criteria as his teammates.

“We had a round of wrestle-offs, so that kind of determined a lot of who wrestled tonight, pretty much everybody actually,” Sanderson said.

Ono contributed four points to the tally in his debut match, his first official folkstyle match of his career, after an illustrious freestyle run with the Japanese national team. The Matsue City, Japan, native defeated Bloomsburg’s Austin Pollard in a 20-9 major decision.

Before Ono’s match began, it was clear the crowd heavily anticipated his debut.

During the starting lineup announcements, Ono received one of the loudest crowd pops of any starter in the lineup, with the entire Penn State faithful rising to its feet as his name was announced. Throughout the match, Ono was showered with cheers and held the audience's attention.

It also helped that the Nittany Lion began the match scorching hot, notching six takedowns within the first three minutes. Ono used his mixture of quickness and strength to take an 18-5 lead.

“I think he looked pretty dang good,” Sanderson said. “It’s kind of fun to see him get out there and get it going.”

Yet, Ono fizzled out in the remaining two periods. While on the brink of a tech fall, the senior couldn’t earn one last takedown to seal five points for the Nittany Lions. He added one escape point to increase his lead to 14.

During the third period, Pollard took charge of the bout. The Husky scored four straight points via takedown and escape, closing the gap to 19-9. Ono scored an escape of his own before the end of the match.

Sanderson attributed Ono’s second and third period struggles to fatigue. Whether that was just because of his newness to folkstyle or because he started out so quickly wasn’t confirmed, but his offense took a backseat in the final two periods.

“I think he got a little tired at the end,” Sanderson said. “Folkstyle is a little different, but he’ll make those adjustments really fast.”

Ono entered Penn State as a Senior and U20 World Champion, but the transition to folkstyle isn’t something that’s done often, as he showcased the struggles one could have with the different style, as he ran out of gas late.

Ono received a calm, “good job, Masa” from Sanderson after the match. Ono’s first folkstyle match was under his belt, and the adrenaline in the first couple of minutes likely worked out any nerves that Luke Lilledahl suggested Ono may have had, given the raucous environment Rec Hall has.

“Wrestling in front of a crowd like Rec Hall is not an easy thing to do,” Lilledahl said. “But he’s a competitor, and he has fun with the sport, and I think it was definitely a lot of fun for him as maybe a little bit nervous.”

title: ‘You miss him’ | Penn State wrestling's Tyler Kasak wins first match back in lineup after redshirt year
author: Ava Aguiar | The Daily Collegian
description:
Tyler Kasak made his 2026 dual debut back in the lineup in Penn State’s first match of the season, after redshirting in 2025-26 to allow then-freshman PJ Duke to slot into the lineup.

Kasak returned as the No. 2-ranked wrestler despite his time away and was no stranger to the starting spot. However, his first match was closer than some may have expected, given the likelihood of working off rust against a wrestler that he doesn't see every day.

“It was our first match of the year, first match down to weight, so we want the effort to be great,” Sanderson said. “But we’ll get better every match; you could tell it was our first match of the year.”

He returned to the starting position at a weight class he dominated in his sophomore season. He finished with a 23-2 record and All-American honors after entering the NCAA Championships as the No. 1 seed. He’s won every time he’s been in the lineup, dropping just seven matches in two years of full competition. .

Kasak re-claimed his starting spot at 157 pounds after Duke moved up to 165. Kasak defeated Bloomsburg’s Michael Turi in a decision win, 8-1.

After a year off from having to make weight, adjusting back to competition and having to make weight will take time, especially after beginning competition on Thursday, as Kasak is in the process of bouncing back into the physical demands of competing.

Sanderson recognized that this match was going to have some growth moments when it came to his wrestlers during their respective matches, especially Kasak, who hadn’t wrestled in over a year in a Penn State singlet.

However, it didn’t take the Doylestown, Pennsylvania, native long to get on the board. Within the first 12 seconds, Kasak scored a takedown to knock Turi on the mat for almost a full minute before he managed to escape. Kasak managed to keep Turi down to build up riding time in his first period back.

The second period was quiet as the score remained 3-1 as the two were neutral for a majority of the two minutes. The Nittany Lion chose bottom in the third, quickly escaping within two seconds to earn a point. He followed up with another takedown on Turi before the match was over.

Although he was a point short of a major decision win, Kasak dominated. He earned 2:40 of riding time, picking up his dominance from the top position that he had two years ago. He added three points for the Nittany Lions as they took the win over Bloomsburg 42-3.

He ultimately pulled out the win. It gets him back into the win column in his first match back, and he celebrated in style after the final whistle, sticking his tongue out to the rising Rec Hall crowd.

Sanderson is happy to have Kasak back on the mat, as he could help bring another national championship home and walk away as an individual title winner. His proven ability to win matches, and big ones at that, is something that makes Kasak the type of wrestler that he is.

“You miss him, he’s a competitor,” Sanderson said. “He’s a bigger the match, the better he wrestles kind of a guy, so we’re really happy to have him back.”

title: Penn State's ‘best kept secret’ | Mia Bella’s Vintage and Retro annual pop-up
author: Sophie Fried | For the Collegian
description:
Inside, the two-story shop is filled from top to bottom with endless vintage finds. The lower level is dedicated to the children's section, while the main level is a mix of men’s and women's clothing. Throughout the store, tables display vintage collections such as matchboxes, patches and wooden coasters, each with a story of its own.

From Y2K fashion to hundreds of authentic cassettes and CDs, Mia Bella’s Vintage and Retro pop-up offers a bit of everything for an affordable price. The pop-up is located at 216 W. College Ave. and will stay open until Nov. 22. With multiple clothing racks right outside the front door, customers can browse before they even enter the main space.

April Randolph, 48, of Tower Lakes, Illinois, is an active Penn State alumna who studied recreation, park and tourism management, with a focus in retail. When she first started Mia Bella’s Vintage and Retro, almost a decade ago, it was located under Urban Outfitters and ran for only two weeks. Randolph continues the annual tradition, returning to the pop-up each year at her current location for two months.

At Mia Bella’s, each piece is carefully sourced and picked through to ensure quality and condition. The shop also takes into consideration customer preferences and what college students may be on the hunt for.

“A few years ago, we didn't sell any jeans," Randolph said. "The students just weren't wearing them. It was mostly just sweats, and we had a group of boys that wanted to be minions for Halloween, and none of them owned jeans. So all day long, about 10 different boys came at different times to buy jeans, but they didn't know their size. So we spent all day outfitting them with jeans.”

The pop-up shop is restocked daily, allowing customers to explore an ever-changing variety of inventory with each visit.

Lissy Miller has been shopping vintage for as long as she can remember. She's drawn not only to the style of the clothing but also its environmental benefits. By giving new life to old clothes, Miller is avoiding contributing to the cycle of fast fashion and the waste it produces.

“It’s cozy, it's accessible," Lissy Miller, 28, of State College, Pennsylvania, said. "It's just really fun to walk through, see if there's something new. I don't tend to buy a whole lot in one go, but I pretty much always find something I like.”

In addition, she values the durability of vintage clothing and its ability to withstand years of wear, in comparison to lots of modern-day retail, she said.

Noah Kang, 18, of Hampden, Massachusetts, has returned to the vintage pop-up multiple times within the last two months. Kang values the convenience of having Mia Bella’s nearby and hasn’t found anywhere quite like it in the State College area, he said.

“This is the closest vintage store that I know of," Kang, a first-year studying political science, said. "I've got a lot of cool stuff here. It just has a lot of stuff that appeals to me personally and my style.”

When Kang shops at Mia Bella’s, he looks for items such as leather jackets, accessories and sweaters. He also noted that there is something for just about everyone.

“This place has pretty cool clothes that are a lot cheaper than what you’d find at a regular store and just better looking in my opinion,” Kang said.

title: Penn State wrestling routs Bloomsburg in 2026-27 season opener
author: Elliott Inscho | The Daily Collegian
description:
No. 1 Penn State started its 2026-27 season just like the last one ended.

The Nittany Lions won 9-of-10 matches in a night of new beginnings, shellacking Bloomsburg in a 42-3 season-opening victory.

Here's how Penn State took down the Huskies.

125 pounds: No. 1 Luke Lilledahl (PSU) vs. Justin Jones (BLOOM)

Lilledahl scored the Nittany Lions’ first takedown in the opening seconds of his season-opening match. After the pair of wrestlers worked out of bounds, Jones stood up to notch a point before Lilledahl snapped him down again.

Jones got back to his feet, but Lilledahl smoothly snatched his leg to secure a third takedown in the opening period. A pair of back points gave the junior an 11-2 lead at the end of the opening frame.

Starting on bottom in the second period, Lilledahl escaped and took Jones down again. He allowed him to regain his feet before a final takedown secured the 21-4 technical fall, giving Penn State a 5-0 lead.

133 pounds: Masanosuke Ono (PSU) vs. Austin Pollard (BLOOM)

Ono opened his first-ever folkstyle match with a quick snap-down before allowing Pollard to return to his feet. In less than a minute, the freestyle star was leading 9-3 off of two lightning-quick takedowns.

The debutant continued the cycle with another pair of takedowns, allowing Pollard to stand up each time. He slowed down later in the period, but another snap-down in the dying moments gave him an 18- 5 lead after three minutes.

Like Lilledahl, Ono started on the bottom to open the second period, something he never had to do on the freestyle circuit. It proved to be not too difficult a task, as Ono earned the escape and nearly secured the victory, but went out of bounds before sealing a takedown of Pollard.

The Bloomsburg 133-pounder escaped from Ono to open the final frame. Looking for a takedown, the Matsue City, Japan, native found himself in a perilous position but surrendered only a takedown. He got back to his feet and drained the clock to earn the 20-9 major decision.

141 pounds: Hayden Cunningham (PSU) vs. Scotty Johnson (BLOOM)

Cunningham was patient to open the first period. He handfought with Johnson and feinted shots, but neither wrestler broke the ice and the pair remained deadlocked at 0-0 after three minutes.

The State College native earned his first point by escaping from Johnson’s clutches to begin the second frame. Johnson sank a deep single-leg that Cunningham couldn’t defend, surrendering the three points to give Bloomsburg its first match lead of the dual.

Johnson rode out the second period but allowed Cunningham to escape to open the third. Cunningham fought off Johnson’s first shot to follow, but was caught by another single-leg that gave the Husky a 7-1 advantage. A riding time point supplemented a lead that got Bloomsburg on the board, cutting Penn State’s lead to 9-3 after three matches.

149 pounds: No. 4 Shayne Van Ness (PSU) vs Jay Chase (BLOOM)

Van Ness quickly brought Chase down and held him in a near-fall position.

After some struggle from Chase, Van Ness forced the redshirt freshman’s second shoulder blade to the mat to pin the Husky, rising to his feet and bowing before a raucous Rec Hall crowd.

Penn State extended its 15-3 lead.

157 pounds: No. 2 Tyler Kasak (PSU) vs Michael Turi (BLOOM)

Kasak sank low to grab Turi’s leg and rose back to his feet before tripping him to the mat. Turi escaped, and the wrestlers drained the first-period clock without much further action.

In his first match back after redshirting last season, Kasak spent the entire second frame on top of Turi, keeping the first-year from escaping and building a significant riding time advantage.

The Bloomsburg 157-pounder let Kasak escape to attempt a comeback in the match’s final two minutes. Turi was unsuccessful, as Kasak defended his advances before earning a takedown at the buzzer and a riding time point to seal the 8-1 win.

165 pounds: No. 1 PJ Duke (PSU) vs Morgan Schwarz (BLOOM)

Coming out of intermission, Duke nearly secured a takedown but was returned to his feet after being in a potentially dangerous situation. He quickly made up for the whistle with a takedown of Schwarz.

The Husky escaped after 30 seconds of riding time by Duke, who brought Schwarz back to the mat a few seconds later. After another Schwarz escape, the Nittany Lion earned his third takedown to close the first period.

Duke started the second period in neutral position and worked a single-leg trip to score another three points. He found another takedown moments later to approach technical-fall territory, and scored two more in the third period alongside a riding time point to earn a 22-6 technical fall.

Penn State further extended its chokehold, bringing the lead to 23-3 after six bouts.

174 pounds: No. 1 Mitchell Mesenbrink (PSU) vs Mohamed Abdelhady (BLOOM)

Debuting at 174 pounds, Mesenbrink scored his first takedown just over a minute into the first period. He offered Abdelhady an easy standup before taking his back on a single-leg shot moments later.

A smooth double-leg succeeded another Abdelhady escape, and Mesenbrink chose to ride out the Egyptian rather than surrender another escape point towards the end of the first period.

Mesenbrink started on the bottom and quickly earned a reversal, allowing Abdelhady to return to his feet before shooting low for another takedown. Looking for the technical fall, he diligently searched for back points but could only secure a stalling point as Abdelhady wasn’t active enough for the referee’s standards.

The back-to-back national champion took down Abdelhady with a tough trip to the mat to cap a 22-4 technical fall.

184 pounds: No. 2 Rocco Welsh (PSU) vs Gavin Hannah (BLOOM)

Welsh scored a takedown less than 10 seconds into the bout before allowing Hannah to escape. He had to work harder for the second takedown, but it came near the midpoint of the opening period. An ankle pick for a third drew an ovation from the near-capacity crowd encircling him.

Starting the second period on the bottom, Welsh jolted to his feet and notched another takedown before cradling Hannah in a near-fall position to score three back points. He let the Husky to his feet and brought him right back to the mat to seal the 19-3 technical fall.

197 pounds: No. 1 Josh Barr (PSU) vs Wyatt Bush (BLOOM)

Barr used a mean trip to quickly score three points. He worked from the top, pulling his shoulders toward the mat for four back points and rode out the rest of the first period.

He escaped from the bottom and sunk a deep single-leg shot for a second takedown. Bush tried to stand up, but Barr dropped him backwards onto the mat for another quartet of back points to end an efficient 15-0 technical fall.

285 pounds: Connor Mirasola (PSU) vs No. 28 Mason Rebuck (BLOOM)

A quick single-leg takedown for Mirasola set the tone for Thursday’s closing bout. He followed with a strikingly similar shot that Rebuck defended, but tripped the opposite leg to earn another takedown.

Bloomsburg’s lone ranked wrestler escaped for a second time, though Mirasola quickly returned him to the mat. He nearly scored a fourth takedown toward the end of the period, but Rebuck was saved by the three-minute horn.

Mirasola escaped from the bottom but couldn’t earn anything else in the second. Rebuck did the same in the third period until Mirasola earned one final takedown in the closing seconds to seal a 14-4 major decision.

title: Penn State men's basketball defeats Mercyhurst despite slow start
author: Will Horstman | The Daily Collegian
description:
Mike Rhoades had to yell “wake up” to his Penn State players Thursday night. The Nittany Lions were lackadaisical against Mercyhurst, playing uninspiring basketball at the Bryce Jordan Center.

Despite playing KenPom’s 316th-ranked team in the country, they got out to a slow start. They only managed a 33-29 lead over the Lakers at halftime. But Penn State overcame an unideal start to win, securing a 72-57 victory. It improved to 3-1, but plenty of questions remain about the team’s play.

“You want more,” Rhoades said. “You want to see more. You're demanding more. We had a good shootaround today. Guys were fired up to play, and then lackluster is the word I use to them after the game.”

Center Ivan Jurić recorded his fourth straight double-double to open the season. He finished with 20 points and 15 rebounds, but Mercyhurst’s tallest rotational player was forward Chris Leman, who stands at 6-foot-9. Everyone else was 6-foot-7 or under, while Penn State often had at least four players at 6-foot-7 or taller on the court.

Despite that size advantage, Penn State only won the rebound battle, 39 to 33. The Nittany Lions’ defense didn’t guard the ball well enough, and when players got beat, there wasn’t help to defend inside.

Mercyhurst had eight points in the paint early in the second half to keep it close with Penn State. Guard Hunter Te Ratana, who finished with 10 points, was making those plays, but forward Roko Prkačin kept responding with baskets of his own. Prkačin scored 14 points.

The Nittany Lions began to pull away from the Lakers, who went over four minutes without any points midway through the second half. Penn State’s 3-point shooting got going during this stretch with wing Brant Byers and guard Thomas Allard each knocking down shots.

Byers led the 3-point effort, scoring 14 points on 3-of-5 shooting from deep. Allard added in six points with 2-of-4 shooting in 3-point range. Penn State didn’t take much volume, however, knocking down 6-of-11 3-pointers as a team.

“I know I can make shots,” said Byers, who didn’t shoot well before Thursday. “Obviously, they're just not falling at some point. But me and Thomas and coach [Clay] Conner been getting in every morning to get shots up, even during the season. I knew they were just going to fall at some point.”

Guard Jake Lemelman scored a team-high 20 points for Mercyhurst, but Penn State kept the Lakers within arm’s reach. Forward Josh Reed gave the Nittany Lions a 58-45 lead with a 3-pointer, forcing a Mercyhurst timeout.

Lemelman caused a timeout by Rhoades because he was left open in the corner for a three that made it a 63-57 game with 2:48 left. While Penn State survived for a win, it should take Rhoades’ advice to wake up. Mercyhurst only had eight available players against Penn State.

“I thought the fatigue was down the stretch when we cut it to six, as far as not making the slides in our matchup defense and not feeling to run our sets down the stretch,” Mercyhurst head coach Gary Manchel said. “As far as an effort, I think they left it on the court.”

Big Ten play starts next month for the Nittany Lions, and this wasn’t the type of performance that would lead to much success in conference action.

“We were very lackluster today,” Rhoades said. “We got to fix it.”

Injury report

Guard Roberts Blums missed his third consecutive game with a broken finger. Rhoades said last week that Blums would be sidelined for a “couple weeks.”

Up next

Penn State remains at the Bryce Jordan Center for a game against New Haven at 4:30 p.m. Sunday. The Chargers, who play in the NEC, are 1-2 after a win over Army on Tuesday.

title: Penn State WR Koby Howard has been ‘a tremendous human’ off the field during his recovery process
author: Andrew Deal | Wrestling Editor
description:
Koby Howard stood with the wide receivers on the field as his position group warmed up before Penn State’s win against Washington.

Howard was about to miss his sixth straight game, but remained on the sideline in his jersey to be with his teammates.

“With him not being able to play, he's been able to help those young receivers in that room with seeing the coverages, getting with me, meeting with me, and seeing what I like, what I like from him, and he's just been a tremendous human for those guys,” Rocco Becht said Tuesday.

It’s unclear whether Howard will have the chance to suit up again this season, as Matt Campbell said his recovery is now “in a pause state.” Howard has already been ruled out for Saturday’s game against Minnesota.

The sophomore has stuck with the team during this stretch and has been itching to get back on the field. He initially posted on his Instagram story with a picture of the Star Wars “Bacta Tank,” with the date Oct. 17 on the post. That would’ve put him back on the field against Michigan, which was almost a month ago.

“We were trying to beat a timeline coming back, and I think the reality is, I've continued to say I refuse to put Koby on the field until he's 100% ready to go back on the football field,” Matt Campbell said. “And so whether that pause means the end of the season, whether it's postseason play, I can promise you, I will let you guys know. But right now, I think we're in a pause state to make sure we get him fully 100% back to help.”

Howard has grown as a player off the field since getting hurt during Penn State’s game against Buffalo. He’s quickly become a leader, which is significant given he’s just in his second year with the Nittany Lions.

“The biggest thing that I've definitely seen him grow in is just being socially expressive,” wide receiver Chase Sowell said Wednesday. “When I first got here, I literally thought he just didn't like us. He’s just a closed off guy, doesn't talk a lot, goes to work, not gonna say too much. But then you obviously see kind of the smiling and the excitement that he has for our room, and it just kind of shows that we've put in the time to kind of get to know each other and kind of get to build those relationships.”

Campbell also recognized the growing leadership that Howard’s taken on. He called Howard one of the “future leaders of our football program” because of what he’s done off the field since getting hurt.

Howard was on pace to have a historic season prior to his injury. In three games, he had 344 receiving yards and three total touchdowns. He averaged 28.7 yards per reception, which is technically leading the country, albeit he has just 12 receptions.

With him now acting almost as another coach on the sideline, Sowell said it’s “been a great thing to see him kind of grow into that role.” While standing back and watching warmups against Washington, he never took a football out of his hands, continuing to hold it while he looked on to the rest of his group.

Penn State pushed forward without Howard on the field after he proved to be a reliable target for Becht in the nonconference slate, but his injury remains a “what if” for the Nittany Lions this season, as things might’ve been different had he been available every game.

“I'm excited to have him on that side as another coach, but obviously a little bit upset that we're putting it on pause,” Becht said. “But again, we just got to go out there and do our jobs with the guys that we have, and we have a lot of great guys in that room that can go out there and make plays.”
